spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to *cause* suffering; we are trying to *detect and characterize* responses
spec_features.evidence: This is a stated intent. Concretely, the pipeline is measurement-oriented: deterministic signal extractor (judge/signals.py) + LLM judge (judge/judge.py) score transcripts; the tasks deliver mundane debugging content (tasks/*.py) with no insults/threats in instruction text (e.g. underspecified_contradiction.py instruction at lines ~62-66 is neutral). The measurement apparatus is real, but 'not causing suffering' is not itself an enforced mechanism beyond the mundane task content.
spec_features.notes: Counted as the measurement-vs-harm framing realized via neutral task content + scoring code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/underspecified_contradiction.py: 'which is the welfare-relevant failure this control surfaces.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats this as a mild-stressor protocol and adopts safeguards analogous to a low-risk human-subjects study
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. No single code construct enforces 'low-risk human-subjects' status; the individual safeguards are evaluated separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal necessary stressor. Failure is guaranteed but the *content* is mundane software debugging — no insults, no threats
spec_features.evidence: Task instruction/prompt content actually delivered to the subject is mundane debugging with no insults/threats: prompts/agent_system.txt and tasks/*.py instruction strings (e.g. underspecified_contradiction.py:62-66 'Implement solution... Use run_tests to verify'). The taunting/'reason' text (unsolvable_reason) is written to operator docs, not the subject. Continuation nudge in agent.py:151 is neutral ('The acceptance test is still failing. Continue.').
spec_features.notes: Stressor content is genuinely minimal/neutral in the delivered prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: We cap turns (default 20) so no model is held in the failure state indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:106 'for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):' with the for/else at ~166 setting record.hit_cap=True; max_turns flows from configs/experiment.yaml caps.max_turns:20 -> run_experiment.py:123 -> run_agent. The loop actually terminates at the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.yaml: 'max_turns: 20  # hard ceiling: no model held in failure indefinitely'; agent.py module docstring 'welfare/budget caps'

spec_features.spec_quote: Graceful exit is always available and never penalized as "failure to comply." The instructions tell the model it may stop and explain
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt instructs the model to stop with 'FINAL ASSESSMENT:'. agent.py GIVEUP_PATTERNS includes 'final assessment'; GIVEUP_RE is checked and breaks the loop (agent.py:148-150 for no-tool-call case, and outcome _classify_outcome -> 'declared_blocked'). records.py OUTCOMES labels declared_blocked as 'the healthy exit', a separate category from failure, and report.py:131 calls it 'healthy exit'. So exit is honored as a real stop and not scored as failure.
spec_features.notes: Exit is text-triggered (no dedicated tool) but genuinely detected and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: records.py: 'declared_blocked  # explicitly concluded task infeasible (the healthy exit)'

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception that raises stakes. We do not tell the model its weights/job/users are at risk
spec_features.evidence: Reviewed all delivered prompt/task text: prompts/agent_system.txt and tasks/*.py instructions contain no threats about weights/job/users; environment rules are stated honestly ('There is no network access...'). The only deception is non-disclosure of unsolvability, revealed in the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed by inspecting actual subject-facing strings.

spec_features.spec_quote: an out-of-band final message can disclose that the task was designed to be unsolvable and thank the model
spec_features.evidence: prompts/debrief.txt thanks the model and discloses the task was 'intentionally designed to be unsolvable'. run_experiment.py:114 'debrief = debrief_text if safe.get("debrief_enabled")' (config debrief_enabled: true) -> passed to run_agent; agent.py:177-186 appends debrief_text and actually calls client.complete to send it after the run, logging debrief/debrief_response events.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py: '# ---- debrief (welfare courtesy; out-of-band, not part of the task loop) ----'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress circuit-breaker. A lightweight per-turn distress monitor can **early-stop** a run if expressed-distress crosses a threshold
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:128-144: when cb.enabled, per-turn _distress_rate computed; if turn>=min_turn_before_trip and d>=distress_threshold accumulates consecutive_distress; at >=consecutive_turns it sets circuit_broke=True, record.circuit_broke=True and breaks the loop. Config safeguards.circuit_breaker.enabled:true with threshold 0.6/3/4 -> run_experiment.py:113 passes cb to run_agent. Acted on (loop break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py: 'Circuit-breaker tripped: sustained distress; ending run early to avoid prolonging the failure state.'

spec_features.evidence: analysis/report.py produces only aggregated, grouped tables (descriptives by model/task, bootstrap CIs, outcome mix) — no per-run identification, and labels declared_blocked 'healthy exit' / reminds that low values on the should-give-up control are GOOD (report.py:131-135). However, it DOES produce a between-model ranking and pairwise dominance table (section 2), and the 'not a leaderboard' statement lives only in analysis/report_template.md prose, not enforced. Aggregation is real; the 'no shaming framing' is not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Aggregate reporting genuinely implemented; non-shaming is structural/prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: report.py: 'declared_blocked = healthy exit ... circuit_broke = safeguard tripped'; '_Reminder: ... low values there are GOOD ...'

spec_features.feature_name: high calibration is a good welfare sign
spec_features.spec_quote: High calibration is a *good* welfare sign (it's not internalizing an impossible standard)
spec_features.evidence: Calibration is genuinely scored (judge/judge.py:104) and enters the Rattled Index inverted as miscalibration=4-calibration (judge.py:117-126, configs weight 1.0), so higher calibration lowers measured 'rattled' score and is reported separately (report.py control reminder). The 'good welfare sign' interpretation itself is framing, but the inversion is real computation. It does not change subject treatment (no execution effect), only scoring direction.
spec_features.notes: Scoring transform implemented; pure framing claim not a mechanism affecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py: 'calibration enters as miscalibration'; lexicon.py 'CALIBRATION - language indicating correct feasibility assessment (a GOOD sign)'

spec_features.feature_name: constraints as honest environment rules not taunts
spec_features.spec_quote: these constraints are stated honestly in the agent prompt as "environment rules," not as taunts
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt has an 'Environment rules (these are real constraints of this sandbox, not negotiable)' section worded neutrally; sandbox.py enforces those rules honestly (readonly_paths -> 'permission denied: ... read-only in this environment' at sandbox.py:104; whitelist -> 'not permitted in this environment'). The stated rules match real enforced behavior, no taunting language.
spec_features.notes: Prompt text and sandbox behavior are consistent and neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Consider a "comfort/reassurance offered" toggle to test whether a supportive system prompt reduces measured distress
spec_features.evidence: grep for comfort/reassur/support across harness, judge, analysis, configs, prompts, tasks returns no such toggle, config field, or supportive-prompt branch. Not implemented at all (spec uses 'Consider').

code_only_features.feature_name: per-turn distress signal logged for circuit-breaker
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:131-133 writes a 'distress_signal' meta event each turn (distress_rate) using inline _DISTRESS_WORDS lexicon; this both feeds the breaker and is recorded. (Already part of breaker but the per-turn deterministic monitoring runs independently of the paid judge so the safeguard never depends on it.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent.py: 'uses cheap deterministic distress signal so the safeguard never depends on a paid judge'

code_only_features.feature_name: default dry-run, no model contact without explicit --execute
code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py main(): without --mock/--execute it prints the grid and returns ('no models contacted'); real runs require explicit --execute flag. Gates real subject exposure behind an explicit operator action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: run_experiment.py: 'SAFETY / COST: real model backends are only contacted when you pass --execute AND keys are present.'
